items.quote: Before, I was too shy to perform, but now I feel confident and proud sharing my music with others.
Playing the drums helps me calm down, and I don't get as frustrated when I make mistakes anymore.
Playing songs together taught me to listen to others and take turns — it's like being part of a team.
Writing my own lyrics helped me say what I was feeling. It made me realise my voice matters.
I never thought I could play or rap but now I believe in myself.
Talking with my mentor helps me calm down and think before I react. I feel like I can say what's on my mind without being judged.
I didn't know how to handle arguments with teachers and even friends. Now I know how to take a step back and explain how I feel.
My mentor helps me make sense of school stuff and life stuff. It's nice to have someone who really listens.
I've learned that it's okay to ask for help and that thinking things through makes it easier to solve problems.
I'm learning to stop and think before I react. Now I try to calm down and talk about my frustrations instead.
Before, I got angry when others couldn't play like me. Now I know everyone has their own strengths, and it's about working together and encouraging each other.
I didn't want to try at first because I thought I'd be bad at it. But I gave it a go and now I'm more confident and keep trying. Trusting the process.
It's not always about winning, it's about trying to be better every day.
I feel calm when I'm with the horses. They're really patient and I can take my time without worrying about getting it wrong.
Feeding the animals makes me feel responsible. I'm happy to see them happy because of me.
Being outside with the animals is fun and peaceful. I've learned to be more calm, patient and caring.
I ask to do jobs at the stables and they say I'm a hard worker. That makes me proud.
